Literature can be broadly categorized into two main areas based on whether intermediate cues are employed: direct methods and two-stage pipelines. In the latter category, CNN regresses intermediate cues such as object coordinates or virtual control points instead of pose parameters in the initial stage. Object pose is then resolved through the construction of correspondence constraints utilizing these intermediate cues. We studied an array of Type IIB four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ effective field theories to uncover the range of universal symmetries potentially present and then investigated why they are avoided. Generalized $\theta$-terms emerge as crucial elements in these theories. These $\theta$-terms generate nonlinear connections between axion fields and quadratic gauge field strengths which can be used to break many universal symmetries. This often misplaced trust is the foundation on which our objective is built – namely to minimize the reliance on device hardware and software components for users to withstand cyber threats. 

We introduce an innovative multi-domain hardware setup consisting of isolated sections, where programs are partitioned statically to prevent malicious interaction. 

A few key hardware components with proven security functionality are integrated to grant secure temporary access to processing resources and external input/output interfaces simultaneously.

To manage these hardware components, we introduce OctopOS, a unique OS comprising several secure subsystems working together in distrust. 

We showcase a functioning prototype, incorporating our hardware and software, utilizing a combined CPU-FPGA board with an acceptable additional hardware expense in comparison to existing SoCs. 

We observe substantial reduction in trust requirements for security applications using our device, delivering better security performance compared to existing solutions, such as Android, and providing secure operation for a wider range of applications. 

Our hardware and software approach outperforms CleanOS, EnerOS, Haven, HiveOS, and OASIS by utilizing a smaller overall device size, reducing time consumption for security evaluations by over two orders of magnitude, increasing secure security application performance by up to nine times, and supporting both Android and iOS operating systems. 

We also examine monetary costs associated with manufacturing our hardware, estimating production expenses of approximately $350 for the required hardware components, with potential future reductions

rose formalism, the use of bivectors plays a key role in identifying the precise solutions to Einstein's field equations. This review focuses on explaining the fundamental principles and detailed calculations of bivectors within the Newman-Penrose formalism, specifically by converting a complex self-dual electromagnetic field from the standard Minkowski space basis to the complex null tetrad basis. As a result, we derive the complex coefficients of the Weyl tensor in the context of Newman-Penrose formalism. This complex coefficient is shown to be directly linked to the electromagnetic field strength in four-dimensional spacetime. Furthermore, we demonstrate that in the presence of a cosmological constant, the complex self-dual electromagnetic field leads to the creation of 'hedgehog' gravitational instantons. This review also explores alternative methods to determine the complex coefficients of the Weyl tensor and confirms that the Newman-Penrose formalism offers a more straightforward approach. Lastly, we outline the application of our findings to related problems. This review is intended to be an educational resource for researchers who may not be familiar with the Newman-Penrose formalism and its use in describing gravitational fields via electromagnetic field analogies. As such, the discussion includes the fundamental principles of the Newman-Penrose formalism, the conversion of electromagnetic field components, and the derivation of the complex coefficients of the Weyl tensor. This review is complemented by an appendix containing the general transformation rules for the Newman-Penrose formalism.

CT scans can be very difficult for humans or computer systems due to low contrast, the varying shape of the esophagus, and the presence of external objects such as feeding tubes. To compensate for these difficulties, doctors often rely on supplementary information from other imaging techniques, medical histories, and endoscopic findings. Acquiring and combining these sources of information is time-consuming and sometimes produces inconclusive results. In this study, we investigate the potential for a more streamlined clinical approach that solely utilizes CT scans for automatically identifying and outlining tumors in the esophagus with satisfactory precision. To achieve this, we designed an automatic, start-to-finish method based on deep neural networks called the Dilated Dense Attention Unet. This model leverages spatial and channel attention mechanisms in dense blocks to prioritize specific features and regions. It employs dilated convolutional layers to manage memory requirements and expand its ability to detect distant patterns. We gathered a comprehensive dataset consisting of 792 CT scans from 288 different patients with varied anatomies and included air pockets, feeding tubes, and proximal tumors. To test the robustness of our network, we conducted repeat studies on different training samples. Our model produced a dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.79, a mean surface distance of 5.4 mm, and a Hausdorff distance of 14.7 mm for 287 test scans. These results demonstrate the efficacy of a simplified, CT-only approach in accurately identifying and outlining esophageal tumors.

This work introduces Hypatia, an interior-point solver designed to handle these complex shapes with ease. In regions of high star formation rates within the galaxy, the mass ejected through outflows actually exceeds the amount of gas converted into new stars, indicating a limit on how quickly gas can be turned into stars due to outflows. A previously developed approach by Baker achieved PTAS on various graph classes including planar graphs. Further, Romero, Wrochna, and Zivny developed a simpler PTAS for certain graph classes using the Sherali-Adams LP relaxation for maximum CSPs with constraints defined by arbitrary non-negative functions.

This research is extended to CSPs with constraints that have multiple possible values. The only restriction for such constraints is that they contain an element that is at least as acceptable as all other elements.

A new PTAS is presented for general-valued CSPs with constraints that have distinct values, such as 0 and 1, but with specific limitations. The technique was previously applicable to classes where Baker's approach worked, except possibly fractionally-treewidth-fragile classes. The findings relax the monotonicity condition of the constraints, allowing a new property called diagonalisability. The appearance of this property is linked to a new NP-approximability measure. The research also shows that PTAS can be achieved for certain graph classes that do not meet the diagonalisability property, using an alternative technique. The results provide a new framework for understanding the behaviour of CSPs on various graph classes. The research is published at the 39th International Conference on Machine Learning. Although machine learning models have been successful in detecting false information, especially when large amounts of labeled data are available, their effectiveness significantly declines when they are applied to emerging events. This limitation creates a significant obstacle for the current methods in detecting false news on unexpected events. Furthermore, the fact that newly emerging events necessitate building a new model from scratch or retraining the existing one, which is often expensive, time-consuming and impractical in real-world settings. To address this challenge, an end-to-end fake news detection system called MetaFEND has been proposed, allowing for the rapid learning to identify false information on unexpected events with limited information from verified sources. This system utilizes a dual-path neural network architecture that combines a convolutional neural network and a recurrent neural network, extracts relevant features from the article content and the posting user's history, and fuses the extracted features for a robust classification. Moreover, two innovative meta-learning algorithms, namely MetaFEND-NN and MetaFEND-NN++, have been designed to facilitate efficient training and accurate performance. These algorithms leverage the system's end-to-end design, a deep network architecture, and a limited amount of labeled data from the verified sources. An extensive experimental evaluation of the proposed system and the meta-learning algorithms was conducted on two large-scale datasets collected from Twitter and Reddit. Current methods of weather prediction, using either a network of sensors or a vehicle-mounted camera, are limited in scope and costly.
A robust weather detection system is crucial for seamless operation of transportation services in diverse weather conditions.
However, this task is complex due to the varied nature of weather and the scarcity of distinct characteristics that distinguish different weather conditions.
Existing approaches to this problem are largely confined to specific environments and only tackle the classification of two weather types.
In this study, we introduce the RFS dataset, which includes images representing three categories of weather (rain, snow, and fog), and propose a novel algorithm utilizing super-pixel masks for data augmentation to yield satisfactory results using multiple Convolutional Neural Network configurations. 
Our primary goal is to develop a general-purpose weather detection system capable of identifying three distinct weather conditions. 
We further aim to evaluate the generalizability of our algorithm across different datasets and neural network architectures. 
Following best practices in machine learning, we employ a diverse set of training and evaluation methods, including the use of multiple initial models and thorough analysis of classification matrices. 
Our experiments demonstrate that our proposed approach yields optimal results and can be adapted for use on mobile devices. 
We discuss the implications of our research and explore potential paths for further improvement. 
We have made our code and dataset available for other researchers to build upon this foundation. 
We plan to share our methodology with manufacturers to enable the integration of our weather detection system into production vehicles.

A plasma source with a 0.1 meter length and 0.4 meter diameter provides plasma necessary for the experiment, and features a helical antenna to produce high-density plasma in the helicon mode of discharge.
